signature.name: San Diego Zoo
signature.detail: One of the world's most celebrated zoos, home to pandas, elephants and a huge collection set in Balboa Park's canyons. Buy tickets online in advance for a discount, and arrive at opening to beat the crowds and heat.

signature.name: Balboa Park
signature.detail: A sprawling cultural park with museums, gardens and Spanish colonial architecture, and the zoo sits within it. Go on a weekday morning, wear comfortable shoes, and use the free tram to get around.

signature.name: USS Midway Museum
signature.detail: Tour a decommissioned aircraft carrier docked downtown, with planes on deck and crew quarters below. Book online, allow at least three hours, and go early to avoid the midday sun on the flight deck.

signature.name: La Jolla Cove
signature.detail: A scenic cove with sea lions, tide pools and clear water for snorkeling and kayaking. Visit early morning for fewer crowds and better wildlife viewing, and keep a respectful distance from the sea lions.

signature.name: Coronado Beach
signature.detail: A wide, golden-sand beach with the historic Hotel del Coronado as its backdrop. Take the ferry or drive over the bridge, and go in the late afternoon for softer light and fewer people.

signature.name: Cabrillo National Monument
signature.detail: A clifftop monument with sweeping views over the harbor, the city and the Pacific, plus a historic lighthouse. Drive or take a rideshare to Point Loma, and come on a clear day for the best views.

signature.name: Old Town San Diego
signature.detail: The historic birthplace of the city, with adobe buildings, museums and Mexican restaurants. It is easy to reach by trolley; go on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds.

signature.name: San Diego Harbor Cruise
signature.detail: A boat tour of the harbor showing the skyline, naval ships and the Coronado Bridge from the water. Book a late-afternoon departure for cooler air and good light, and bring a light jacket for the breeze.

transport: Trolley or bus $2.50 a ride; rideshares moderate
